task.description:
Read ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis in full at handoffs/WF03-ISS0451-20260904/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnosis.json (result.summary) -- it confirmed empirically (real code read plus a live throwaway probe) that a PERSISTENT Poller fault cascades from Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers' own budget exhaustion (max_restarts: 5, max_seconds: 60) into the top-level Letflow.Supervisor's default OTP restart budget (3 restarts / 5 seconds, never overridden in lib/letflow/application.ex) within about 96ms wall-clock, taking down the whole application (Repo, Bandit included) -- the exact incident REQ-219 exists to prevent, just for a persistent rather than single-shot fault.

Produce a design artefact in lib/letflow/design/ (follow this project's existing convention, e.g. lib/letflow/design/req219-supervision-layering.md's shape) choosing and fully specifying a fix. ISS-0451's own description names two candidate options, neither prescribed: (a) raise the top-level Letflow.Supervisor's own restart intensity so it tolerates at least one full Pollers-budget-exhaustion cycle without exiting itself, and/or (b) give Pollers a circuit-breaker/backoff so a persistent fault degrades to a stopped-but-not-crash-looping state rather than repeatedly re-exhausting its own budget and repeatedly costing the top level a restart. You choose the design -- this is a real architectural decision with an availability tradeoff (see the design considerations below), not a default to pick without reasoning.

Design considerations to work through and document (this is what ISS-0451's AC2 requires -- concrete arithmetic, not just a chosen number):
- If you raise the top-level's restart intensity alone: what value tolerates at least one full Pollers-exhaustion-and-restart cycle (Pollers' own 5-in-60s budget means Pollers can legitimately exit and be restarted by the top level at most once per 60s under NORMAL bounded-transient-fault operation before Pollers' own budget resets -- but under a PERSISTENT fault, Pollers re-exhausts almost immediately after each restart, so the top level would need to tolerate MANY such Pollers-exits within its own window, not just one, unless something also slows the retry rate). State the exact max_restarts/max_seconds you choose for the top level and show the arithmetic for why it survives a persistent fault indefinitely (or for how long, if not indefinitely) rather than merely surviving one extra restart.
- If you add a circuit-breaker/backoff to Pollers instead (or in addition): what state machine, what backoff schedule, what makes it degrade to 'stopped, not crash-looping' rather than continuing to consume top-level restart budget at all. Consider that Pollers currently holds TWO independently-gated poller GenServers as peers (Letflow.Scheduler.Poller and Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller) -- a circuit-breaker design must state whether it applies per-poller or to the whole Pollers supervisor, and why.
- Whichever you choose (or if you choose both), the design must not weaken REQ-219's own AC2 (boot-order: Infrastructure before Pollers, structural via list order) or AC4 (single-crash isolation: Pollers exhausting its budget once must still leave Infrastructure/Http alone) -- state explicitly how your design preserves both.
- The design must specify exactly what test(s) TEST-DESIGNER will need to write: a regression test simulating a PERSISTENT Poller fault (never cleared, unlike REQ-219's AC4 test) proving Letflow.Supervisor (top-level), Letflow.Repo, and the Bandit listener all remain alive after Pollers repeatedly exhausts its budget -- name the exact mechanism the test will use to keep the fault persistent (a test-only flag, following the existing force_poller_crash precedent in pollers_test.exs, or something else) and what observable proves the top-level supervisor never exited (e.g. Process.whereis(Letflow.Supervisor) staying the same pid, or a monitor).

This is a design artefact ONLY -- no implementation code, no .ex file changes outside lib/letflow/design/. Signatures/specs/config-value choices only, per this project's design-vs-implementation convention (see CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own gate criteria, which will check for implementation code present and fail the gate if found).
acceptance_criteria: Design artefact created under lib/letflow/design/, named appropriately (e.g. iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md)
Design states the exact top-level restart-intensity value chosen (if that lever is used) with the arithmetic showing it tolerates at least one full Pollers-budget-exhaustion cycle, per ISS-0451 AC2
Design states the exact circuit-breaker/backoff mechanism (if that lever is used) with its state machine and thresholds
Design explicitly confirms REQ-219 AC2 (boot order) and AC4 (single-crash isolation) are preserved and states why
Design specifies the exact test mechanism and observable(s) for the new persistent-fault regression test
No implementation code (.ex function bodies) present in the design document -- signatures/specs/config values only
task.rework_note: REWORK ITERATION 2: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-gated your iteration-1 revision and FAILed it again, with 4 BLOCKERs, all downstream of ONE root cause (full text in handoffs/WF03-ISS0451-20260904/step-02b-code-design-validator.json's result.issues -- read it there for exact line numbers). Root cause: your revised design's children-list entry in section 3.4a, `{Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary}`, does NOT actually apply restart: :temporary to Pollers' child spec. Elixir's Supervisor.init/2 treats a 2-tuple {module, arg} children-list entry as 'call module.child_spec(arg)', threading arg as the START_LINK ARGUMENT, not as Supervisor.child_spec/2 override keys -- the validator verified this both statically (against lib/elixir/lib/supervisor.ex's own init_child/1, lines 816-833 and child_spec/2, lines 934-943 in this project's pinned Elixir 1.20.3) and with a live probe. Your intent (top level structurally cannot auto-restart Pollers) is correct and was independently confirmed AS A CONCEPT -- only the syntax expressing it is wrong. FIX: use `Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary)` as the children-list entry itself (i.e. the list element IS the result of calling Supervisor.child_spec/2, not a {module, arg} tuple) -- the validator confirmed live that this corrected form produces a genuine restart: :temporary spec and genuinely suppresses top-level auto-restart. Once you fix section 3.4a's snippet, you MUST re-derive/restate every place that depended on the broken syntax, not just patch the snippet in isolation: section 3.6/3.7/4's 'exactly 0, structurally unconditional' arithmetic (re-verify it now genuinely holds under the corrected form -- expected to, but must be re-checked, not assumed); section 5's AC4-preservation claim (it currently states the existing pollers_test.exs AC4 test 'will fail as written' once Pollers is :temporary -- under the broken syntax that claim was actually false, since the top level still auto-restarted; re-confirm whether it becomes true again under the corrected syntax, which is expected, and restate the reasoning); section 6.2 step 6's test observable (`Process.whereis(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers) == nil` while breaker is :open -- only valid once the corrected syntax is in place, re-verify). Finish this handoff normally per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4 (status COMPLETED, full result block, completed_at from the real clock) -- this rework note does not suspend or change that normal completion step.

result.summary: REWORK ITERATION 2 complete. Fixed lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md section 3.4a's children-list syntax from the broken `{Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary}` (a 2-tuple {module, arg} form, which Supervisor.init/2 normalizes as 'call module.child_spec(arg)', threading arg into start_link -- confirmed live, no :restart key results, defaults :permanent) to the corrected `Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary)` used directly as the children-list entry -- confirmed live (Elixir 1.20.3, this project's pinned toolchain) that this form genuinely produces a %{..., restart: :temporary} spec, and that a supervisor started with it never auto-restarts a killed child, its which_children goes empty, and the PARENT supervisor's own restart-intensity counter is untouched (0/1 max_restarts survived 10 kill cycles). While re-deriving the downstream sections per the rework note (not merely re-asserting), discovered and fixed a SECOND, previously-unflagged defect that only surfaces once the child spec is genuinely :temporary: Supervisor.restart_child/2 cannot restart a :temporary child that has already exited once, because OTP deletes a :temporary child's spec the instant it terminates (confirmed live: restart_child/2 on an already-exited :temporary child returns {:error, :not_found}, not a fresh pid). This breaks every restart call the design specifies for PollersBreaker (the :closed-branch handler on 1st :DOWN, and the :half_open_probe handler) -- both corrected to Supervisor.start_child/2 with the full child spec, confirmed live to work correctly and repeatably across cycles, and to safely no-op with {:error, {:already_started, pid}} if called while the child is still alive. This same defect also breaks the EXISTING test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs test's own restart_pollers!/0 helper (terminate_child/2 then restart_child/2 -- confirmed live that terminate_child/2 on a :temporary child also deletes its spec immediately, so the helper's own {:ok, _pid} = restart_child(...) match would raise MatchError once Pollers is :temporary), used both inline in the AC4 test body and in its on_exit teardown -- flagged as a required fix for that helper, separate from and in addition to updating the AC4 test's own assertions to expect PollersBreaker's mechanism. Re-derived (not re-asserted) sections 3.6/3.7/4's 'exactly 0, structurally unconditional' top-level-restart-consumption arithmetic against the corrected start_child/2-based mechanism -- still holds, now backed by a live probe showing 10 kill/start_child-restart cycles never touched a max_restarts:1 top-level supervisor. Re-derived section 5's AC4-preservation claim -- the existing test still 'fails as written' once Pollers is genuinely :temporary (this time verified against a genuinely-:temporary spec, not assumed), plus the newly-discovered restart_pollers!/0 helper consequence is now stated explicitly. Re-derived section 6.2 step 6's Process.whereis(...) == nil observable -- still correct, confirmed live against the corrected form; also corrected step 3's test procedure (it referenced the now-broken restart_pollers!/0 shape) and step 6's stray restart_child/2 mention. All ~20 occurrences of restart_child/2 in the mechanism description were audited; each was either corrected to start_child/2, left as accurate historical description of the prior iteration's defect, or confirmed already correct (the terminate_child/restart_child pattern's role as 'not needed to stop a :temporary child' at section 3.4's own paragraph, which does not depend on which restart call is used). No implementation code (.ex function bodies) added -- the only code-shaped content is throwaway probe snippets (a trivial ProbeCD.Worker GenServer) used to demonstrate/verify OTP's own Supervisor.child_spec/2 semantics, consistent with this design's existing convention of citing live-verified evidence, not part of the PollersBreaker/Pollers implementation itself (which remains signatures/types/state-shape only throughout).
result.next_action: Re-gate with CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step-02b) against this rework-iteration-2 revision.

gate_history.summary: Prior attempt's design chose a PollersBreaker circuit-breaker (2-consecutive-:DOWN trip) plus a top-level max_restarts 3->5 raise, with margin arithmetic '5 - 2 = 3' assuming the breaker's terminate_child call always beats the top-level Supervisor's own automatic restart-on-exit for the same child exit. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently re-derived this and found the assumption unproven -- see handoffs/WF03-ISS0451-20260904/step-02b-code-design-validator.json result.issues[0] for the full BLOCKER text.
issues: Unproven race: PollersBreaker's monitor-message-then-terminate_child chain is strictly longer than the top-level Supervisor's direct in-process EXIT reaction, with no cited ordering guarantee it wins; section 3.6 was cited as resolving this but analyzes a different race instead.
gate_history.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER: either make Pollers' child spec restart: :temporary so the top-level Supervisor cannot auto-restart it at all (breaker becomes solely responsible via explicit restart_child), or cite an actual OTP ordering guarantee and re-derive the margin arithmetic under the real worst-case restart count.

gate_history.summary: Iteration-1 revision chose restart: :temporary on Pollers' child spec (correct concept, confirmed by the validator against Elixir's own Supervisor source) but expressed it via children-list syntax {Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary}, which does not actually apply the override -- Supervisor's 2-tuple {module, arg} children-list form threads arg into the start_link argument, not into child_spec override keys. Verified live (both statically against lib/elixir/lib/supervisor.ex and via a running probe) that this syntax silently keeps Pollers :permanent, so the original iteration-0 race is unresolved, and 3 further sections (3.6/3.7/4's arithmetic, 5's AC4-preservation claim, 6.2 step 6's test observable) all inherit the same defect since they depend on the broken snippet's claimed effect.
issues: 4 BLOCKERs, full text in handoffs/WF03-ISS0451-20260904/step-02b-code-design-validator.json's own result.issues -- root cause is one syntax defect in section 3.4a, propagating downstream.
